concerns.text: Success Rate is defined as `valid_solutions / (total_instances - excluded_instances)`. Excluding instances where the symbolic planner fails (FR‑006) changes the denominator for the symbolic condition only, inflating its success rate relative to the neural baseline which has no exclusions. This makes the validation target (success rate) dependent on a predictor (planner success) and biases the two‑proportion Z‑test comparison.

The primary hypothesis test uses a two‑proportion Z‑test assuming independent samples, yet both methods are evaluated on the *same* set of puzzle instances. This violates the independence assumption; a paired test (e.g., McNemar’s test or a mixed‑effects model) would be more appropriate for comparing success rates on matched instances.
